meta.title: Furifont: furigana built into the font
meta.description: A Japanese font that shows furigana by itself. The text does not change.

editable: Sample text. You can edit it.

hero.body: Furifont is a Japanese font that shows furigana by itself. Furigana are the small letters above a kanji (a Chinese-style character) that tell you how to say it. The text stays plain. When you copy it, search it, or have it read aloud, you get the exact text that you wrote.

playground.textHint: Click the text to edit it. The font alone makes the ruby.
playground.pasteNote: Paste it anywhere. Only the text that you wrote comes with it.

runs.title: One group of kanji at a time
runs.body: A browser gives Japanese text to a font in separate parts. One part holds only kanji. The font cannot see the kana (the simple Japanese letters) next to it. So Furifont reads each group of kanji as one whole.

longest.title: Longest word first
longest.body: Furifont compares each group of kanji with a list of thousands of common words. It tries the longest word first. For example, it picks 日本語 before 日本. It reads 今日 as one word, きょう.

bare.title: No ruby when unsure
bare.body: A single kanji gets ruby only when one reading is clearly the most likely. 大人気 can be read だいにんき or おとなげ, so Furifont shows no ruby.

pick.title: Readings you can choose
pick.body: A word can have more than one reading. Put a variation selector after the first kanji of the word to choose another reading, or to remove the ruby. A variation selector is an invisible character. It stays when you copy and paste.

selectors.body: Some words have more than one common reading. Furifont shows the most common one. To choose another, put a variation selector (an invisible character) right after the first kanji. VS226 gives reading 1, VS227 gives reading 2, and so on. VS225 removes the ruby.

downloads.buildOwn: Or build your own font. You can choose another base font, a list with fewer or more words, other ruby letters, or other sizes.
downloads.cliBuild: a font from the command line
downloads.cliDev: the studio: change the settings, preview, build the font

anyPage.body: You can use Furifont on any website. Lines with kanji get extra space for the ruby. If Furifont is installed on your computer, nothing downloads. If it is not, the font loads from this site. It is about 5 MB the first time.
anyPage.bookmarkletHint: Drag it to your bookmarks bar. On any page, click it to turn Furifont on. Click it again to turn Furifont off. Some sites, such as X and GitHub, do not let fonts load from other sites. On those sites, install Furifont on your computer.
anyPage.userscriptHint: This works with Tampermonkey or Violentmonkey (browser add-ons that run small scripts). It turns Furifont on by itself on Japanese pages. It also works on sites that do not let fonts load from other sites. Its menu lets you switch to another Furifont font or turn it off.

toast.message: Furifont could not load its font on this page. Some sites, such as X and GitHub, do not let fonts load from other sites. On those sites, you must install Furifont on your computer.

reference.title: Pick a reading
reference.body: Furifont shows the most common reading of a word. To show another reading, put a variation selector (an invisible character) right after the first kanji of the word. VS226 gives reading 1, VS227 gives reading 2, and so on. After a single kanji, the selector chooses the reading of that kanji. VS225 shows the kanji with no ruby.
reference.search: Search a word or kanji: 市場, 今日, 生
reference.hint: Click a reading to copy the word with its selector.
reference.unavailable: The reference comes with the ready-made fonts, and it could not load here ({error}). Build the fonts with {command}, or open the studio.

offline.title: Build your own Furifont
offline.body: The studio is a tool that runs on your computer. It reads your base fonts and saves the fonts that it builds. Start it in any folder. Then this page opens with a live preview, the dictionary, and a Build button. The new fonts go in {folder}.
offline.needs: You need Node 22.18 or later (a free program that runs JavaScript tools).
offline.run: Start the studio in any folder

auth.title: Enter the code from your terminal
auth.body: {command} showed a six-digit code in your terminal (the window where you started it).
auth.failed: That code did not work. Check the terminal and try again.

options.baseHint: The font to add ruby to. Use a font to download, such as Source Han Serif JP Bold, or the path to another font file on your computer.
options.skipHint: These words get no ruby, because a reader already knows them. The newspaper word list is sorted by how often the words appear, in steps of 500 words.
options.wordsHint: The next words in the list. With the word lists below, {count} words get ruby.
options.jlptHint: Words on the JLPT lists (for the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test) up to this level get no ruby. N5 is the easiest level.

spec1.name: Everyday words
spec1.hint: JMdict "spec1": common words that the other lists miss, such as 日本.

ichi1.name: Basic words
ichi1.hint: JMdict "ichi1": the most common words from the Ichimango list (a list of basic words).

news1.name: Newspaper words
news1.hint: JMdict "news1": the 12,000 words that appear most often in newspapers.

gai1.name: Loanwords
gai1.hint: JMdict "gai1": common words that Japanese borrowed from other languages.

places.name: Place names
places.hint: JMnedict: stations and places. Furifont uses them where no common word matches the text.

options.shareHint: A single kanji gets ruby only when one reading makes up at least this share of its uses in the dictionary. Use a number from 0.5 to 1. A higher number gives ruby to fewer kanji.
options.resetHint: Go back to the settings that the studio loaded. Your words stay.

dictionary.search: Search the dictionary: 今日, 生
dictionary.hint: These words have several common readings. Pin one to make it the default reading.
